source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: Then, after some time, a demon named Sumali wandered throughout the entire mortal world, having come from Rasatala.
verses.2: He, resembling a dark cloud and adorned with earrings of molten gold, took his daughter, who was as beautiful as Lakshmi without her lotus.
verses.3: While the king of demons was wandering on the surface of the earth, he then saw Kubera, the lord of wealth, traveling in the Pushpaka chariot.
verses.4: Having seen him, the powerful son of Pulastya (Kubera), who was going to see his father, resembling an immortal, moving freely, and radiant like the sun.
verses.5: Having returned to Rasatala from the mortal world, the great-minded Sumali, filled with wonder, began to ponder in this manner.
verses.6: The Rakshasa then spoke to his daughter, Kaikasi by name, pondering how they might prosper and what good they should do.
verses.7: O daughter, this is the time for your marriage, and your youth is passing; you are not being accepted by suitors, who are afraid of rejection.
verses.8: For your sake, all of us, though righteous-minded, are troubled, for you, O daughter, are indeed endowed with all virtues, like the goddess Shri herself; indeed, the fatherhood of a daughter is a sorrow for all who desire honor.
verses.9: And it is not known, O daughter, who would choose to marry such a maiden.
verses.10: O daughter, you are indeed endowed with all virtues, like the goddess Shri herself; a daughter always keeps three families—her mother's, her father's, and the one to which she is given—in a state of uncertainty.
verses.11: O daughter, you yourself should choose and resort to Vishravas, the excellent and best of sages, born in the lineage of Prajapati and son of Pulastya.
verses.12: O daughter, without a doubt, your sons will be like this lord of wealth (Kubera), equal to the sun in splendor.
verses.13: Having heard that instruction, the maiden, out of respect for her father, approached the place where Vishravas was performing penance and stood there.
verses.14: O Rama, in the meantime, the brahmin Vishravas, son of Pulastya, performed the Agnihotra ritual, appearing like a fourth sacred fire himself.
verses.15: Disregarding that dreadful time, out of respect for her father, the beautiful maiden approached and stood before him, her face bowed towards his feet, repeatedly scratching the ground with the tip of her big toe.
verses.16: The exceedingly noble sage, having seen her, who had beautiful hips, a face like the full moon, and was shining with her own radiance, spoke to her.
verses.17: O gentle lady, whose daughter are you, and from where have you come here; O beautiful one, tell me truly what your purpose is or for what reason you are here.
verses.18: Thus addressed, the maiden, having folded her hands, then spoke, saying, "O sage, you are capable of knowing my intention by your own spiritual power."
verses.19: "But know me, O Brahmarshi, as one who has come by the command of my father; I am named Kaikasi by name, and you are capable of knowing the rest."
verses.20: The sage, having then entered into meditation, spoke these words: "O gentle lady, the reason that was in your mind has been known by me."
verses.21: O you who walk like an intoxicated elephant, since you have approached me at this dreadful time with a desire for a son from me.
verses.22: Therefore, O auspicious one, listen to the kind of sons you will give birth to: they will be terrible, of dreadful appearance, and fond of cruel deeds.
verses.23: O lady with beautiful hips, you will give birth to Rakshasas who perform cruel deeds; but she, having heard his words, bowed down and spoke.
verses.24: O venerable one, O speaker of Brahman, I do not desire such extremely ill-behaved sons from you; please show me your grace.
verses.25: But Vishrava, the foremost among sages, thus spoken to by the maiden, spoke again to Kaikasi, just as the full moon speaks to Rohini.
verses.26: O fair-faced one, your last son will be worthy of my lineage and will be righteous.
verses.27: O Rama, that maiden, thus addressed, after some time gave birth to a repulsive and very terrible Rakshasa-shaped child.
verses.28: The child had ten necks, great fangs, resembled a heap of blue collyrium, possessed copper-red lips, twenty arms, a huge mouth, and blazing hair.
verses.29: At the very moment of his birth, jackals with flaming mouths and other carnivorous animals moved in inauspicious anti-clockwise circles.
verses.30: The sky rained blood, clouds roared harshly, the sun did not shine, and great meteors fell upon the earth.
verses.31: The earth trembled, very fierce winds blew, and even the unshakeable ocean, the lord of rivers, became agitated.
verses.32: Then his father, who was like his grandfather (Brahma), named him Daśagrīva, declaring that this newborn would indeed be Daśagrīva (ten-necked).
verses.33: After him, the immensely powerful Kumbhakarna was born, whose vast size and measure had no equal in this world.
verses.34: Then Shurpanakha, named for her deformed face, was born, followed by Vibhishana, the righteous-souled last son of Kaikasi.
verses.35: Indeed, when that great being (Vibhishana) was born, a shower of flowers fell.
verses.36: Then, drums of the gods sounded in the sky, and a voice from the heavens exclaimed, "Excellent! Excellent!"
verses.37: Then, those two, Kumbhakarna and Dashagriva, grew up in that great forest, becoming exceedingly powerful and a cause of distress to the world.
verses.38: Kumbhakarna, reckless and ever unsatisfied, roamed about, devouring great sages devoted to dharma and causing havoc in the three worlds.
verses.39: In contrast, Vibhishana, a righteous soul, always remained steadfast in dharma, living with self-study, a controlled diet, and mastery over his senses.
verses.40: Then, after some time, the god Vaishravana, the lord of wealth, came there in his Pushpaka chariot to see his father.
verses.41: Having seen him (Kubera) shining with splendor there, Kaikasi, the demoness, came to Dashagriva (Ravana) and indeed spoke to him.
verses.42: "O son, behold your brother Vaishravana, endowed with splendor, and even though you are equal in brotherhood, behold yourself in such a state."
verses.43: "O Dashagriva, O one of immeasurable valor, make such an effort, my son, so that you become equal to Vaishravana."
verses.44: Having heard that speech of his mother, the valorous Dashagriva felt unequalled indignation and then made a vow.
verses.45: "Truly, I promise you that I shall become either equal to or even superior to my brother in might; therefore, abandon the sorrow residing in your heart."
verses.46: Then, filled with that very anger, Dashagriva, along with his younger brothers, set his mind on performing a difficult penance.
verses.47: Having resolved that he would achieve his desires through penance, he then came to the auspicious hermitage of Gokarna for the accomplishment of his own purpose.
verses.48: That demon of fierce prowess, along with his younger brothers, then performed incomparable penance there, and he also pleased the lord Brahma, who, being pleased, granted him boons that brought victory. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे नवमः सर्गः ।। 9 ।। Thus ends the ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
